children.translated_text: I shall expound the <s>Śālistambakakārikā</s> (Verses on the Rice Seedling). //1//

body.translated_text: Having bowed to the fully awakened one, who possesses infinite and inconceivable qualities and whose nature is compassion,

children.translated_text: The sage, on the mountain named <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) near <s>Rājagṛha</s>,
was established together with the assemblies of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) and <s>bodhisattvas</s>. //2//
Having observed a rice seedling arisen from causes and conditions,
[he taught that] likewise, what arises from causes and conditions proceeds through the sequence of the twelve limbs. //3//

children.text: pratītyamiti yaḥ praśyet dharmaṃ buddhaṃ ca paśyati /
children.translated_text: Whoever sees that which is dependently [arisen] sees the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Buddha</s>;
having spoken thus, the leader remained silent among the <s>bhikṣus</s>. //4//
The <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Śāriputra</s>, having heard [this], went into the presence of <s>Maitreya</s>,

children.text: tathāgato 'dya maitreya uktyarthaṃ na vibhajya ca // 5 //
children.translated_text: [saying:] 'Today the <s>Tathāgata</s>, O <s>Maitreya</s>, spoke the meaning but did not analyze it.' //5//

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ bhāve sthitaścātra tadartho gamyate katham /
children.translated_text: 'He has remained in silence here—how then is that meaning to be understood?

children.text: kiṃ pratītyaṃ ca ko dharmo buddho 'pi katamastathā // 6 //
children.translated_text: What is dependent [origination], what is <s>Dharma</s>, and likewise, who is the <s>Buddha</s>?' //6//

children.text: pratītyaṃ tu kathaṃ dṛṣṭvā dharma buddhaṃ ca paśyati /
children.translated_text: 'How, by seeing dependent [origination], does one see the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Buddha</s>?
I have doubt here—please explain,' thus spoke <s>Śāriputra</s> to <s>Ajita</s> (Maitreya). //7//

children.text: bhāvātmikā hi maitrī syāt maitreyo 'brūt nirṇayam /
children.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s>, whose nature is loving-kindness, spoke the determination:
'The twelve limbs beginning with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and ending with death, in sequence— //8//
from those indeed arise merely the aggregates of suffering;
the <s>Dharma</s> is the eightfold path, and the fruit is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>. //9//
Through the complete realization of all this, one [sees] what is born of <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Buddha</s> itself;

children.text: tathoktamāryaṃ duṣṭatvāt yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati // 10 //
children.translated_text: as declared by the Noble One, due to the corrupted nature [of things], whoever sees [thus], truly sees.' //10//
'And one who, from that which is devoid of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) and so forth, endowed with complete cessation,

children.text: pratītyaṃ dharmabuddhau ca śuddhabuddhayā vi paśyati // 11 //
children.translated_text: sees dependent [origination], <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Buddha</s> with purified understanding.' //11//
'Now, the characteristic of dependent [origination], accompanied by the terms cause and so forth—

children.text: buddhotpādo bhavenno vā sthiteyaṃ dharmatā yataḥ // 12 //
children.translated_text: whether a <s>Buddha</s> arises or not, this <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of phenomena) remains.' //12//
'The cause-condition is twofold: external and internal;

children.text: bāhyo hetustu bījādiḥ pratyayaḥ ṣaḍvidho mataḥ // 13 //
children.translated_text: the external cause is the seed and so forth, and the condition is considered sixfold.' //13//
'Just as the seed, sprout, stem, and so forth proceed toward the fruit,
so too the conditions—earth and so forth, ending with time—[proceed] in sequence.' //14//
'Supporting, moistening, ripening, growth of grain, unobstructedness,
and transformation—their function proceeds in that manner.' //15//

children.text: no cet pratyayasāmagrī bīje bhūte 'pi nāṅkuraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If the aggregate of conditions is not [present], even when the seed exists, there is no sprout;
and when the seed is absent, even if conditions truly exist, it is likewise [fruitless].' //16//
'Causes and conditions are likewise devoid of self-grasping and so forth;
through the aggregate of causes and conditions, the fruit of action does not perish.' //17//

children.text: na svato parato nāpi na dvayoḥ kartṛkālataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not from self, not from other, not from both, not from an agent or time,
not made by <s>Īśvara</s> (God) and so forth, not from inherent nature, nor without cause.' //18//

body.translated_text: 'The operation of cause and condition has been manifest from beginningless time;
external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) is accepted as [having] five causes.' //19//

children.text: śāśvatato na coccedān na saṃkranteḥ parīttataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Not from eternalism and not from annihilationism, not from transmigration, from the limited,
from a small cause, great fruition is obtained; from the arising of what is similar.' //20//
'The sprout is regarded as [coming] from the seed; without cause there is no arising of a sprout;
cessation and arising are equal, like the tipping up and down of a balance.' //21//
'Likewise, the cause and condition of the internal [process] is also twofold;
the primary cause is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), [proceeding] in sequence ending with death.' //22//
'The twelve limbs, whose nature is birth, <s>kleśa</s> (affliction), and <s>karma</s> (action), are threefold in division;
arisen from causes and conditions, they are devoid of an agent and so forth.' //23//

children.text: avidyā yadi nādau syādante mṛtyurna saṃbhaved /
children.translated_text: 'If <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) did not exist at the beginning, death would not occur at the end;

children.text: tebhyo bhinno na kutrāpi hyātmātmīyaśca vidyate // 24 //
children.translated_text: apart from those, nowhere whatsoever does a self or what belongs to a self exist.' //24//
'From the arising of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) at the beginning, death appears at the end;
thus, the conditions of the internal [process] are of six kinds.' //25//
'The internal condition at the end is <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), and at the beginning is support;
solidity, cohesion, ripening, respiration, growth, and unobstructedness— //26//
and the continuity of cognition and form, combined with the five consciousnesses;
therefore, the afflicted mind also—these are the internal conditions.' //27//
'From the coming together of the <s>dhātus</s> (elements), the arising of the body is accepted;
the arising of concepts of self and what belongs to self is not considered [to come] from those.' //28//
'When those [conditions] are present, there is arising; when those are absent, there is no occurrence;
they are certainly not made of self and so forth, nor is there anything else whatsoever.' //29//
That which has the designation of a single mass, etc., is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) covering the three realms of existence,
<s>Rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>moha</s> (delusion), etc., arise and exist through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). // 30 //
From that, the cognition of conditioned phenomena arises as <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness),
And together with <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) arise the four formless <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). // 31 //
Depending on <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), the sense faculties and bases arise,
From the conjunction of sense objects, sense faculties, and consciousness, <s>sparśa</s> (contact) arises. // 32 //

children.text: vedanā sparśajā jñeyā tṛṣṇā ca vedanodgatā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vedanā</s> (feeling) is known to arise from contact, and <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) arises from feeling,
The increase of craving is <s>upādāna</s> (clinging), and from clinging arises <s>bhava</s> (becoming). // 33 //
The arising of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) from becoming is <s>jāti</s> (birth), and from birth likewise comes <s>jarā</s> (aging),
The cessation of the <s>skandhas</s> from aging, that is declared to be <s>mṛtyu</s> (death). // 34 //

children.text: mūḍhe tu maraṇācchokaḥ satṛṣṇe dāha āntaraḥ /
children.translated_text: For the deluded one, from death comes <s>śoka</s> (grief); for one with craving, there is inner burning,
That lamentation which arises from grief is called <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental suffering). // 35 //
That which arises from mental suffering, pertaining to the five sense-consciousnesses and the body,
Is called unpleasant <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), which destroys bodily happiness. // 36 //
The suffering called mental affliction, which harms the mind,
That should be known as <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental anguish), which causes other afflictions. // 37 //
Darkness (ignorance), cognition, name-and-form, sense bases, contact, feeling, craving,
Craving, clinging, becoming, birth, decay, destruction, and grief— // 38 //
Lamentation, bodily affliction, and mental anguish likewise,
These are the names declared in order, each meaningful according to its affliction. // 39 //
Again, through the complete understanding of reality, from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) onward in sequence,
The arising of each successive link from each preceding one has been explained. // 40 //
The twelve-limbed chain of dependent origination has three modes of activity; eternalism and annihilationism are both beginningless,
It flows like a stream of water from beginningless time. // 41 //
Nevertheless, these four are the causes that bring about the aggregate:

children.text: avidyā ca tṛṣā karma vijñānaṃ kramaśo matāḥ // 42 //
children.translated_text: <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>karma</s> (action), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) are considered in sequence. // 42 //
The seed of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is indeed the cause, and <s>karma</s> (action) is declared to be the field,

children.text: prathamaḥ ca tṛṣā prokte hetuḥ kleśasvabhāvataḥ // 43 //
children.translated_text: And <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is said to be the primary cause, due to its nature as affliction. // 43 //
<s>Karma</s> (action) and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are established as the seed-nature of consciousness,
And <s>karma</s> performs the function of the field for the seed of consciousness. // 44 //
The seed called <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is moistened by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving),
And <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) scatters the seed of consciousness with its moisture. // 45 //
<s>Karma</s> is the field, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> is the moisture, and <s>avidyā</s> is the scattering,

children.text: vijñāne na karomīdaṃ na vijñānamito matam // 46 //
children.translated_text: In consciousness there is no thought 'I do this,' nor is consciousness considered to arise from this [self]. // 46 //
Nevertheless, when the seed-consciousness is established in <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),
Consciousness is called the seed, scattered in the soil of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). // 47 //
When watered by the water of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), from the cause of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form),
The appearance of the sprout's arising is indeed not from self, other, both, or without cause. // 48 //
This <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) is born from the union of father and mother,
Due to non-obstruction and the season, and pierced by some taste of existence. // 49 //
The seed-consciousness, as it is called, gradually accumulates in the mother's womb,
And the sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) arises through the completeness of conditions. // 50 //
Due to the non-obstruction of causes, in restraining through the selflessness of illusion,
Arising is not to be conceived; thus also for visual consciousness. // 51 //
Visual consciousness is born from five causes: the eye, form, illumination,
Space, and attention born from them; from the completeness of these five. // 52 //
When visual consciousness has arisen, there is no thought 'I have produced you,'
Such conceptualization does not arise, and likewise for auditory consciousness and all others. // 53 //
Thus the process of arising is from the gathering of causes and conditions,
And due to the absence of an agent and such, through separation from ego-sense. // 54 //
Arising proceeds as before, and thus also what is dependently originated,
One should understand as having causes—nothing exists beyond this world without causes. // 55 //
No phenomenon goes anywhere; through causes and conditions likewise,
The fruit of <s>karma</s> (action) approaches, just as in a polished mirror, // 56 //
Face-reflections are seen, yet in the mirror there is no actual image,
Nothing has transmigrated there; that is the non-discrimination of one from another. // 57 //
That arising is devoid of agent and action, yet the appearance of arising is thus,
And it occurs through the sequence of prior growth, just as the moon, though far away, // 58 //
Is seen in a small vessel of water without having moved there,

children.text: asti kriyā ca karmāpi tathā cāsmāccyutirna hi // 59 //
children.translated_text: There is action and <s>karma</s> likewise, yet there is no falling from this existence. // 59 //
The appearance of birth also occurs in the world; just as fire does not arise without fuel,
It blazes fully and brightly, but is diminished by the loss of fuel. // 60 //
The connection of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) would be [thus]; they are of the nature of conceptual construction.
External <s>karma</s> and action are the cause, being dependent on the internal. (verse 61)
Arising from the five <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses), the ultimate reality is beyond investigation.
It is declared to be <s>pariniṣpanna</s> (perfected), arising from causes and conditions. (verse 62)
It should always be known as twofold, and likewise devoid of agent and so forth.
One who thus sees through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) that its essence is emptiness, not mere voidness— (verse 63)

children.text: kiṃ kathaṃ vā kuto kena kalpavādādihānitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "What?", "How?", "From where?", "By whom?"—free from conceptual assertions and the like,

children.text: udacandrasya yathā bimbaṃ tataḥ kaścicca na cyutaḥ // 64 //
children.translated_text: Just as the reflection of the moon in water, from that no one has truly fallen. (verse 64)
Birth too appears in the world, just as [fire] connected with a tree,
The stream of fire would proceed; likewise from the diversity of causes. (verse 65)
For fire does not continue into [the next moment]; likewise regarding the seed of affliction,
When burned by the fire of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), due to the absence of the cause, there is no fruit likewise. (verse 66)
Action and <s>karma</s> do not exist at all; [the Buddha has] infinite and inconceivable qualities,
A body whose nature is peaceful <s>dharma</s>, devoid of beginning, middle, and end. (verse 67)

children.text: jñātvā prāpnoti buddhatvaṃ ya evaṃ tathatākṣamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having known thus, one who is patient with <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) attains <s>Buddhatva</s> (Buddhahood).

children.text: tasmai vyākriyate nūnaṃ maitreyastu svayaṃ tathā // 68 //
children.translated_text: To such a one a prediction is certainly given; thus <s>Maitreya</s> himself [was predicted]. (verse 68)
[He] spoke to <s>Śāriputra</s>: the simile of the rice seedling was thus made.
And <s>Śāriputra</s>, having heard that, was rejoiced by the assembly of <s>devas</s> (gods). (verse 69)
Praised and having grasped the essence, rising and going forth with delight,
He declared [it] to the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks). (verse 70)

body.translated_text: The <s>Āryaśālistambakasūtrakārikā</s> (Verses on the Noble Rice Seedling Sūtra), composed by the noble <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, is completed.

children.translated_text: Translated by the Bhāvatīya preceptor <s>Dharmaśrībhadra</s>, and the great editors <s>Lokacakṣus</s>, <s>Sādhumati</s>, and <s>Jñānakumāra</s>.
Afterwards revised and finalized by the venerable <s>Kuṭīrakṣita</s>.
